extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline (OED/USPTO audiences)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, sanctions, and reinstatement/monitoring conditions imposed in a USPTO OED Final Order for a registered patent attorney who violated USPTO professional conduct rules. Covers violations, prescribed sanctions, required remediation, monitoring, reporting, and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the statutory and regulatory authority under which OED and the USPTO Director take disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable ethical code based on date of events
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the events occurred prior to May 3, 2013, the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.20–10.112) is applicable; effective May 3, 2013, the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines which regulatory provisions and standards are used to evaluate practitioner conduct depending on when misconduct occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to inform client of important Office correspondence (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and (b) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(8) — proscribing failure to inform a client of important Office correspondence when the correspondence (i) could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office, (ii) was received by the practitioner on behalf of a client or former client, and (iii) was such that a reasonable practitioner would believe under the circumstances that the client or former client should be notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED treats omission to notify clients of such correspondence as a breach of professional duty; the three-element test (i)-(iii) guides determination of obligation to notify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neglect of legal matters (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c): proscribing neglect of legal matters entrusted to a practitioner, exemplified here by allowing trademark applications to become abandoned without clients' knowledge or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect includes failing to meet deadlines, allowing matters to be abandoned, and taking remedial action without client permission; grounds for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice (term and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters for five (5) months commencing on the date this Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the duration and scope of the immediate sanction imposed for the misconduct described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probation following reinstatement (duration and practice permissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a twenty-four (24) month period of probation beginning on the date of any decision granting a petition for Respondent's reinstatement; Respondent shall be permitted to practice before the USPTO during his probationary period unless probation is revoked or otherwise removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditionally restores practice privileges post-reinstatement but subjects practitioner to monitoring and potential revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as condition of reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58; the OED Director shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References the regulatory framework governing petitions for reinstatement and OED's processing of such petitions; specific conditions are enumerated elsewhere in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and Public Key Infrastructure ("PKI") certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectively removes electronic credentials and access as part of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining USPTO Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents circumvention of suspension by obtaining new credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain suspended until OED grants petition for reinstatement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall remain suspended from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is discretionary and subject to OED review under regulatory standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for 60 days to facilitate compliance with 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office commencing on the date this Final Order is signed and expiring sixty (60) days after the date this Final Order is signed, with such limited recognition being granted for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term, narrowly tailored recognition to permit the practitioner to take steps required for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monetary remedies: refund and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall refund $5,000 to Client #1; Respondent shall pay costs of $100 associated with this proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial restitution to client and recovery of OED costs are part of the disciplinary sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice monitor letter requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days of the date of this Final Order, Respondent shall provide to the OED Director a letter acceptable to the OED Director from a registered patent attorney in which said attorney agrees to serve as a practice monitor for Respondent during the period of his probation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice monitor must be a registered patent attorney and must formally agree in writing; monitor plays a central role in probation oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly mental health counseling and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agrees to continue to receive counseling from a mental health professional at least once a month during his suspension and comply with all treatment recommendations of the mental health professional, including attending therapy sessions and taking medication as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED conditions reinstatement on ongoing mental health treatment when mental health issues are mitigating/causal factors in misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Releases authorizing disclosure by treating mental health professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agrees to provide to all treating mental health professionals an appropriate release as required under state and federal law authorizing the treating professional to: (a) disclose to the OED Director, as requested, information pertaining to the nature of Respondent's compliance with any treatment plan established; (b) promptly report to the OED Director Respondent's failure to comply with any part of an established treatment plan; and (c) respond to any inquiries by the OED Director regarding Respondent's mental or emotional state or compliance with any established treatment plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver/authorization required to allow OED to obtain compliance information directly from providers; necessary for OED oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness letter from mental health professional
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide to the OED Director a letter from his mental health professional confirming that there is no mental health reason that Respondent is not capable of practicing patent, trademark, and other non-patent law, including having the ability to meet deadlines and communicate with his clients, and that his mental condition is stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED requires professional confirmation of fitness to practice, addressing specific functional abilities (deadlines, communication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent mental health examination if requested and cost reimbursement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent agrees that, if requested by the OED Director, i) he shall submit to a mental health examination to be performed by an independent mental health professional selected by the OED Director in the OED Director's sole discretion, and ii) Respondent shall reimburse the OED Director for all costs associated with said examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED may require independent evaluation and shift the cost burden to the practitioner seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter from legal assistant describing responsibilities and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall provide to the OED Director a letter from his legal assistant setting forth her understanding of her work responsibilities, her weekly work schedule, her experience with trademark and patent prosecution, and her experience with the docketing and calendaring software used by Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED seeks assurance that staff assisting practitioner are competent and that role/responsibilities are clearly defined to prevent future neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diary and docketing system requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall establish and use a diary and docketing system, including a mechanism by which approaching deadlines are noted, that is commonly accepted by patent and trademark professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates adoption of industry-standard calendaring/docketing tools and procedures to reduce missed deadlines and abandoned matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone message system and timely return requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall establish and use a system by which telephone messages are recorded and telephone calls are returned in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures timely client communication and tracking of telephone inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client status request response system
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall establish and use a system by which written requests by clients for the status of their legal matters are answered, either orally or in writing, in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal process required to ensure clients receive timely updates in response to status inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial client fee disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall establish and use a system whereby clients are apprised at the outset of the representation of the basis upon which fees will be calculated and costs paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires upfront disclosure of fee basis and cost obligations to clients to avoid misunderstandings and promote transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly itemized billing for hourly-fee matters
rubrics_metrics.description: For cases in which the fee is to be calculated on an hourly basis, a system by which clients are provided with regular itemized billing statements provided at least quarterly, setting forth the services performed by respondent, the date upon which each service was performed, the time spent by respondent on each service and the amount to be charged to the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific billing content and frequency requirement aimed at accountability and client information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly practice monitor reports during probation (content and deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: During Respondent's probationary period, Respondent shall cause the practice monitor to submit quarterly reports to the OED Director during the period of Respondent's probation, confirming that Respondent is meeting deadlines, communicating with clients, and complying with the requirements set out in paragraphs (6)(A) through (6)(E). Said reports shall be due to the OED Director on January 15, April 15, July 1, and October 1 of the respective calendar year; and a failure to provide the OED Director with said reports shall constitute a per se violation of this Proposed Settlement Agreement and the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies report cadence, required confirmations, exact due dates, and that failure to report is itself a violation enabling enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order to Show Cause and response timeline for probation violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply during probation, the OED Director shall issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to Respondent at the last address of record, and grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines procedural due process steps and a 15-day response window before seeking further suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to USPTO Director for additional suspension up to 12 months
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after the 15-day response period and consideration, the OED Director continues to be of the opinion that Respondent failed to comply, the OED Director shall deliver to the USPTO Director (i) the Order to Show Cause; (ii) Respondent's response, if any; and (iii) argument and evidence, and request that the USPTO Director enter an order immediately suspending Respondent for up to an additional twelve (12) months for the violations set forth in the Joint Legal Conclusions above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes escalation path and potential further sanction for probation violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED's ability to seek further discipline notwithstanding settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing herein shall prevent the OED Director from seeking discipline for the misconduct leading to Respondent's additional suspension pursuant to the preceding paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves OED's right to pursue additional disciplinary actions beyond the terms of this Order if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension is not stayed by review of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the USPTO Director suspends Respondent pursuant to paragraph (0), and Respondent seeks a review of the suspension, any such review of the suspension shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review does not automatically stay the effect of the suspension; practitioner remains suspended during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette: a Notice of Suspension and Probation describing the suspension, the violations (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.77(c) and 10.23(a) and (b) via 10.23(c)(8)), requirements for reinstatement, and probation under supervision of a practice monitor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public notice requirement informs the bar and public of disciplinary action and its basis; sample notice text provided in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Final Order shall prevent the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order: (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct concerning Respondent; and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding against Respondent (i) as an aggravating factor in determining discipline, and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf, and/or (3) in connection with any request for reconsideration pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes clear the Final Order may be used as precedent or aggravating evidence in future matters involving the same practitioner.
